prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat electronic bands at a magic twist angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, opening moiré flat-band quantum matter

statement.case_for: After reading all eight first-round statements and the chair's summary, I keep B009 as my preferred configuration, but I hold it with less confidence than in round 1 and I want the committee to see exactly what I am and am not claiming. The scientific core is narrow and testable: the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted that interlayer tunnelling quenches the Dirac velocity at a discrete set of twist angles, and in 2018 correlated insulating and superconducting states were observed in samples at that angle. A geometric control parameter then turns strong correlations on and off, which is the kind of mechanism that carries over to other moiré platforms (transition-metal dichalcogenides, fractional Chern states). The citation I propose covers the flat-band prediction and the observation of the phases, not the pairing mechanism. The chair asked whether the discovery can be separated from the open mechanism. I think it can, in the same way that the Z2 prediction is separated from the later arguments about 3D materials or applications in the B004 case. Waiting for a pairing mechanism to be agreed may mean waiting indefinitely, and the existence of the correlated states at the predicted angle is not in doubt.
statement.case_against: The honest weaknesses are maturity and credit. The decisive experiments are seven to eight years old, the pairing mechanism is open, and strain and twist-angle disorder make it hard to say how much of the phenomenology is intrinsic. Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Eriksson and Pearce all hold B009 back for the first of these reasons, and I cannot dismiss that this many colleagues weigh it the same way. The credit gap is real as well: Yuan Cao and the other first-year co-authors of the 2018 papers, and parallel experimental groups, are outside the credited names, so the experimental half rests on Jarillo-Herrero as group leader. A citation can be worded to say the group's discovery, but it cannot repair the omission. Against my own earlier framing, I also accept that B004 is the safer choice on maturity and that its omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang is a boundary problem that the other leading configuration, B006, simply does not have.

responses.point: The chair asked whether a flat-band prediction and first observation of correlated and superconducting states can be separated from the open pairing mechanism, and whether the committee is prepared to credit the experiment to Jarillo-Herrero alone without Cao and others.
responses.response: On separation, yes: the citation should name the predicted magic-angle flat bands and the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in the twisted bilayer, and say nothing about whether the pairing is phonon-mediated or electronic. That is a statement about a derived phase and not about the discovery. On Cao, I do not have a clean answer, and I will not pretend that I do. The honest position is that this is the weakest point in the B009 credit, and a committee that cannot accept it should not pick B009. I would accept the pairing with Jarillo-Herrero as the leader of the group that made the observation, but I recognise that a colleague who wants every decisive experimental contribution inside the names will reasonably vote differently.

responses.point: Katori's magic-wavelength condition removed the trade-off between atom number and trap-induced shifts, so the lattice clock is a new concept and not a quantitative refinement of the ion clock, and clock performance has been independently verified across several national laboratories.
responses.response: This is a stronger argument than I gave it credit for in round 1, and it moves me. A condition under which the trapping potential does not perturb the transition is a qualitative idea, not just a lower number, and independent reproduction at several institutes is a stability that B009 does not yet have. I still read the case as sitting nearer to the 2005 and 2012 prizes than the moiré or topological work does, and I would still rank it below B004, but I no longer regard it as merely incremental. That is why I now name B006 as one of my two alternatives, in place of B023, which needs five names that the cap does not allow. My remaining difficulty is that the credit leaks towards ion-clock and other lattice-clock groups, and you have not told me how a citation would draw that line.

responses.point: A narrow citation limited to the quantum spin Hall effect and its first observation answers the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang gap and the 2016 overlap, and the committee should not draw three-dimensional work in.
responses.response: A narrow citation is the best available repair for B004, and if the committee goes there I would support Johansson's drafting. But it does not remove the gap. A prize for the quantum spin Hall effect that names the group that measured edge conduction in HgTe but not the authors of the HgTe proposal is awkward whatever the wording, and narrowing the citation also narrows the reach of the result that makes B004 attractive in the first place. The 2016 overlap I still regard as a legitimate concern, though I accept Eriksson's and Danielsson's point that the Z2 time-reversal class is distinct from the Chern-insulator physics honoured then. I weigh the credit gap more than the overlap, and the two together keep B004 behind B009 in my ranking, though only by a margin that I would not defend against a determined colleague.

responses.point: The cost of an early award is asymmetric, because the committee cannot easily correct it later, and B006 is the only candidate that is simultaneously mature, cleanly attributed and carried by a small group.
responses.response: I take the asymmetry seriously. It is the best argument against B009, and I cannot rebut it with data; I can only say that the opposite error also has a cost, because with moiré physics the leading theorist and the leading experimentalist are both alive and credit gets harder to draw as the field grows. I do not think that is decisive. Lindroth's comparison to the pairing mechanism does show, though, that B009 carries an interpretive risk that B004 and B006 do not, and I treat the committee's preference for maturity as a legitimate scientific judgement and not a reluctance.

responses.point: Sample-to-sample variation is real, the origin of superconductivity and of several correlated states is unsettled, and Olsson would prefer to let the mechanism settle for a few more years, though she would not block B009.
responses.response: Sample variation is a fair point and I do not downplay it, but the reproduction of insulating and superconducting behaviour across many independent groups, using different fabrication routes and substrates, suggests that the discovery claim is robust even where details differ. Where I do concede ground is on the practical effect of strain and disorder on how much of the phase diagram is intrinsic; that supports a citation worded around the existence of correlated states at the magic angle and not any specific phase diagram. I appreciate that Olsson says she would not block B009, and I would extend the same tolerance to B004 or B006 if the committee ends up there.

uncertainties: Whether the committee treats the open pairing mechanism and the youth of the field as a reason to wait; this remains the decisive question between B009 and B004, and I know that most of my colleagues answer it differently from me.
Whether leaving out Yuan Cao and the other experimental co-authors can be justified when the experimental credit is rendered to Jarillo-Herrero as group leader.
Priority of the magic-angle idea relative to earlier band-structure and moiré work is judged from my own recollection and cannot be verified from the supplied text.
How a B006 citation would draw its boundary against ion-clock and other lattice-clock groups, which determines whether I could support it as a fallback.
Whether the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang omission and the 2016 overlap are enough to make B004 weaker than I currently judge; I am less sure of this than I was in round 1.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my provided profile. My documented co-authors and institutions do not include any credited name on the shortlist, and I am a statistical physicist of complex systems, not a moiré, topological or precision-measurement specialist. I do not wish to withdraw from any shortlisted candidate. No new disclosure arises from the first-round exchange. I note the conflict disclosures of Kroll, Olsson, Johansson and Pearce and do not consider them disqualifying for me to weigh.
